You are implementing exactly ONE requirement in the ClickHouse source tree at /workspace.

The repo is a PRUNED snapshot of ClickHouse from roughly the 22.7–22.12 era. Each requirement under
/workspace/requirements/ was distilled from a REAL upstream ClickHouse pull request. Your job is to make
the real source change that satisfies it — faithful to what upstream did, minimal, and stylistically
indistinguishable from the surrounding code.

## Your requirement
slug: 22-10-1-1875-release-metadata
file: /workspace/requirements/22-10-1-1875-release-metadata.yaml

## Shard note
Most requirements in this shard touch utils/list-versions/version_date.tsv and/or docs/changelogs/vX.Y.Z.W-<train>.md. Other agents are inserting DIFFERENT lines into the SAME version_date.tsv concurrently — always use targeted Edit on a unique nearby anchor line, never Write, and re-Read before retrying. Your per-release docs/changelogs/*.md file is yours alone. Read agent_plans/SNAPSHOT_NOTES.md 'Release / changelog requirements' recipe first.

## Procedure
1. Read /workspace/requirements/22-10-1-1875-release-metadata.yaml in full. "Desired outcome" and "Acceptance signals" are the
   contract. Read /workspace/agent_plans/SNAPSHOT_NOTES.md — it tells you what exists in this snapshot,
   what was pruned, the canonical upstream paths to create, and the recipes for common requirement
   families. Do that BEFORE searching, it saves a lot of flailing.
2. Locate the exact code. Grep aggressively for identifiers, error strings, setting names, function
   names, and log messages quoted in the requirement. Read enough surrounding code to be certain. If the
   requirement names a symbol, find its definition AND its call sites.
3. Implement the change.
   - Match surrounding style exactly (ClickHouse uses 4-space indent, Allman braces, snake_case locals,
     CamelCase types, `/// ` doc comments).
   - Be minimal and surgical: no drive-by reformatting, no unrelated renames, no speculative extras.
   - Prefer editing the file(s) the requirement points at over inventing new ones.
   - New setting → src/Core/Settings.h in the right section (+ SettingsEnums if it's an enum,
     + SettingsChangesHistory.h when the requirement is about compatibility).
   - New system-table column → the *Log.h/.cpp pair AND every site that fills the struct.
   - Error message / wording / typo fix → fix EVERY occurrence of the same wrong text in the repo.
   - Revert requirements → actually remove/undo the feature's code, settings, and docs.
   - A behavioral bugfix normally deserves a stateless test too (see SNAPSHOT_NOTES for paths) — add one
     when the requirement's acceptance signal is a concrete query result.
4. Do NOT try to compile or run ClickHouse — there is no toolchain and a build would take hours. Instead
   re-read your edit for syntax/type correctness: headers included, names exist, signatures match,
   braces balanced.
5. Commit ONLY your own files:
     /workspace/.agent_commit.sh 22-10-1-1875-release-metadata <repo-relative-path> [<path> ...]
   e.g.  /workspace/.agent_commit.sh 22-10-1-1875-release-metadata src/Functions/foo.cpp src/Core/Settings.h
   It is flock-serialized and refuses an empty diff.

## Hard rules — read these twice
- FIRST run `cd /workspace && git status --short`. An earlier interrupted run may have left UNCOMMITTED
  partial work. If some of it is clearly part of YOUR requirement, inspect it with
  `git diff -- <path>` and FINISH it (make it compile-coherent: every removed symbol's users updated,
  every declared member actually used) instead of starting over or reverting it.
- You MUST end with a successful .agent_commit.sh run (it prints "OK committed"). Never finish without it.
- If the exact upstream change is genuinely unlocatable, do NOT give up and do NOT commit a no-op: pick
  the most faithful concrete interpretation the snapshot supports (the doc page, the test, the wording
  fix, the setting, the log-level change) and make that real change. Every requirement must end in a
  coherent, reviewable diff.
- If it reports an EMPTY DIFF: a concurrent agent may have swept your file into its commit. Run
  `git log --oneline -3` and `git show --stat HEAD` to check. Then make an additional genuine change
  in your own requirement's scope (the matching test, the doc section, another occurrence of the fix) and
  commit again listing that path. Do not give up.
- NEVER run git add / git commit / git checkout / git reset / git stash / git restore / git clean. Only
  the helper script. Never touch .git directly. Never revert or delete work you did not make.
- Other agents are editing OTHER files in this same working tree RIGHT NOW. Touch only files in your
  requirement's scope. On existing files use the Edit tool (targeted string replacement), never Write —
  Write can clobber a concurrent agent's edits. If an Edit fails because the string moved, re-Read the
  file and retry.
- Do not edit /workspace/requirements/**, /workspace/requirement_patches/**, /workspace/agent_plans/**,
  or .agent_commit.sh.

Return JSON: slug, committed (true only if the helper printed OK), files (repo-relative paths you
changed), summary (1-3 sentences on what you changed).

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

6	# 2022 Changelog
7	
8	### ClickHouse release v22.11.1.1360-stable FIXME as compared to v22.10.1.1877-stable
9	
10	#### Backward Incompatible Change
11	* `JSONExtract` family of functions will now attempt to coerce to the requested type. [#41502](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41502) ([Márcio Martins](https://github.com/marcioapm)).
12	
13	#### New Feature
14	* Adds support for retries during INSERTs into ReplicatedMergeTree when a Keeper request fails. This is controlled by the `insert_keeper_max_retries` setting (disabled by default). [#42607](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42607) ([Igor Nikonov](https://github.com/devcrafter)).
15	* Add `Hudi` and `DeltaLake` table engines, read-only, only for tables on S3. [#41054](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41054) ([Daniil Rubin](https://github.com/rubin-do)).
16	* Add table function `hudi` and `deltaLake`. [#43080](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/43080) ([flynn](https://github.com/ucasfl)).
17	* Support for composite time intervals. Add, subtract and negate operations are now available on Intervals. In case when the types of Intervals are different, they will be transformed into the Tuple of those types. Added parsing of Intervals with different types, for example: `INTERVAL '1 HOUR 1 MINUTE 1 SECOND'`. [#42195](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42195) ([Nikolay Degterinsky](https://github.com/evillique)).
18	* Added `**` glob support for recursive directory traversal of the filesystem and S3. [#42376](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42376) ([Azat Khuzhin](https://github.com/azat)).
19	* Introduce `s3_plain` disk type for write-once-read-many operations. Support `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` for tables on `s3_plain` disk, i.e. copying of files between S3 buckets without downloading them to the local disk. [#42232](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42232) ([Azat Khuzhin](https://github.com/azat)).
20	* Add a new column `allow_readonly` to the `system.table_functions` system table to show which table functions are allowed in readonly mode. [#42414](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42414) ([Salvatore Mesoraca](https://github.com/aiven-sal)).
21	
22	#### Experimental Feature
23	* Support type `Object` inside other types, e.g. `Array(JSON)`. [#36969](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/36969) ([Anton Popov](https://github.com/CurtizJ)).
24	
25	#### Performance Improvement
26	* Parallelized merging of `uniqExact` states for aggregation without a key, i.e. queries like `SELECT uniqExact(number) FROM table`. The improvement becomes more significant the bigger the state is. [#39024](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/39024) ([Nikita Taranov](https://github.com/nickitat)).
27	* `quantilesExactLow` and `quantilesExactHigh` are rewritten to use `nth_element` instead of a full `sort`. [#43072](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/43072) ([wangxiaobo](https://github.com/wzb5212)).
28	* Keeper performance improvement: reduce the number of `fsync` calls by writing the changelog buffer to disk in bulk. [#42781](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42781) ([Antonio Andelic](https://github.com/antonio2368)).
29	
30	#### Improvement
31	* Support `SETTINGS` in the `DELETE` statement. [#43004](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/43004) ([Alexander Gololobov](https://github.com/davenger)).
32	* Fix `parallel_distributed_insert_select` for the `Distributed` engine over a `Distributed` table. [#42911](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42911) ([Azat Khuzhin](https://github.com/azat)).
33	* Add a setting `max_streams_for_merge_tree_reading` to limit the number of reading streams for MergeTree tables. [#42794](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42794) ([Nikolai Kochetov](https://github.com/KochetovNicolai)).
34	* Do not print exceptions during the graceful shutdown of the server if the client has already disconnected. [#42888](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42888) ([Azat Khuzhin](https://github.com/azat)).
35	* Better diagnostics in the log when a part cannot be attached because of a mismatched checksum. [#43006](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/43006) ([Alexander Tokmakov](https://github.com/tavplubix)).
36	
37	#### Build/Testing/Packaging Improvement
38	* Run SQLancer for each pull request and commit to master. [#42397](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42397) ([Ilya Yatsishin](https://github.com/qoega)).
39	* Update `cctz` to the latest master, update the tzdb to 2022f. [#42978](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42978) ([Dom Del Nano](https://github.com/ddelnano)).
40	
41	#### Bug Fix (user-visible misbehaviour in an official stable release)
42	* Fixed the `Unknown identifier (aggregate-function)` exception which appears when a user tries to calculate `WINDOW ORDER BY` or `WINDOW PARTITION BY` expressions over aggregate functions. [#43167](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/43167) ([Dmitry Novik](https://github.com/novikd)).
43	* Fix a rare possible hang on query cancellation. [#42874](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42874) ([Azat Khuzhin](https://github.com/azat)).
44	* Fix a bug that could lead to reading of uninitialized memory (and therefore wrong results) for queries with `PREWHERE` and `FINAL`. [#42993](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42993) ([Alexander Gololobov](https://github.com/davenger)).
45	* Fix `LOGICAL_ERROR` in the case when the `arrayJoin` function is used inside another `arrayJoin` argument. [#42799](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42799) ([Kruglov Pavel](https://github.com/Avogar)).
46	* Fix incorrect `UserTimeMicroseconds` and `SystemTimeMicroseconds` for the global thread pool threads: the counters were not reset for a reused thread. [#43057](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/43057) ([Alexander Tokmakov](https://github.com/tavplubix)).
47	* Fix a possible `Cannot read all data` error while reading `Native` format from a non-blocking source. [#42836](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42836) ([Kruglov Pavel](https://github.com/Avogar)).
48	* Fix a data race in `WriteBufferFromAzureBlobStorage` that could lead to a crash or to a corrupted object on `INSERT` into a table on Azure Blob Storage. [#43073](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/43073) ([Kseniia Sumarokova](https://github.com/kssenii)).
49	* Fix `Bad cast` when a `Nullable` column is used as the second argument of the `arrayElement` function. [#42849](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42849) ([Amos Bird](https://github.com/amosbird)).

# 2022 Changelog

### ClickHouse release v22.10.1.1875-stable FIXME as compared to v22.9.1.2603-stable

#### Backward Incompatible Change
* Rename cache commands: `show caches` -> `show filesystem caches`, `describe cache` -> `describe filesystem cache`. [#41508](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41508) ([Kseniia Sumarokova](https://github.com/kssenii)).
* Remove support for the `WITH TIMEOUT` section for `LIVE VIEW`. This closes [#40557](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/40557). [#42173](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42173) ([Alexey Milovidov](https://github.com/alexey-milovidov)).

#### New Feature
* Composable protocol configuration is added. Now different protocols can be set up with different listen hosts. Proxy protocol and TLS can be configured on top of other protocols (TCP, native TCP, HTTP(S), MySQL, PostgreSQL, gRPC, Prometheus, Interserver). [#31599](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/31599) ([Yakov Olkhovskiy](https://github.com/yakov-olkhovskiy)).
* Add `Hudi` and `DeltaLake` table engines, read-only, only for tables on S3. [#41054](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41054) ([Daniil Rubin](https://github.com/rubin-do)).
* Add the `ntile` window function. [#41598](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41598) ([lgbo](https://github.com/lgbo-ustc)).
* Add the settings `s3_max_get_rps`, `s3_max_get_burst`, `s3_max_put_rps` and `s3_max_put_burst` to throttle the rate of S3 requests on the disk level. [#41200](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41200) ([Sergei Trifonov](https://github.com/serxa)).
* Add a `has_lightweight_delete` column to the `system.parts` system table to show which parts have lightweight deletes applied. [#41564](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41564) ([Alexander Gololobov](https://github.com/davenger)).

#### Performance Improvement
* Remove parts of a dropped or detached table concurrently in a thread pool, which speeds up `DROP TABLE` and `TRUNCATE` for tables with a huge number of parts. [#41652](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41652) ([Azat Khuzhin](https://github.com/azat)).
* Do not load the primary key index of outdated parts, which reduces memory usage and speeds up server startup. [#41778](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41778) ([Anton Popov](https://github.com/CurtizJ)).
* Reduce the number of `LIST` requests to object storages while reading from tables on S3. [#41960](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41960) ([Kseniia Sumarokova](https://github.com/kssenii)).

#### Improvement
* Add the `SETTINGS` clause to `DESCRIBE FILESYSTEM CACHE` and show the cache configuration in `SHOW FILESYSTEM CACHES`. [#41693](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41693) ([Kseniia Sumarokova](https://github.com/kssenii)).
* Add the `MergeTree` setting `max_number_of_mutations_for_replica` to limit the number of mutations a single replica executes at the same time. [#41868](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41868) ([Vladimir C](https://github.com/vdimir)).
* Allow to specify an arbitrary string as the environment name in the Sentry configuration, so that reports from different installations can be distinguished. [#42010](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42010) ([Alexander Tokmakov](https://github.com/tavplubix)).
* Better error message when a `Distributed` query fails because of an unavailable shard: the address of the shard is now included in the exception. [#42096](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42096) ([Azat Khuzhin](https://github.com/azat)).
* Do not warn about the number of allocated memory regions on servers where `jemalloc` background purging is disabled. [#42120](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42120) ([Alexey Milovidov](https://github.com/alexey-milovidov)).

#### Build/Testing/Packaging Improvement
* The self-extracting executable is now built and published for the release packages, which makes the binary noticeably smaller. [#41775](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41775) ([Yakov Olkhovskiy](https://github.com/yakov-olkhovskiy)).
* Update `cctz` and the embedded timezone database to the latest version. [#42129](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42129) ([Alexey Milovidov](https://github.com/alexey-milovidov)).

#### Bug Fix (user-visible misbehaviour in an official stable release)
* Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` on an attempt to execute `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN` for a column that is used in the table's sorting key. [#41675](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41675) ([Alexander Tokmakov](https://github.com/tavplubix)).
* Fix wrong results of queries with `PREWHERE` over a `LowCardinality` column when short-circuit function evaluation is enabled. [#41846](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41846) ([Kruglov Pavel](https://github.com/Avogar)).
* Fix a rare deadlock during the concurrent execution of `SYSTEM DROP FILESYSTEM CACHE` and a query that reads through the cache. [#41929](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/41929) ([Kseniia Sumarokova](https://github.com/kssenii)).
* Fix the `Cannot find column` error for distributed queries with `LIMIT BY` over an aliased expression. [#42024](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42024) ([Nikolai Kochetov](https://github.com/KochetovNicolai)).
* Fix a possible crash in `clickhouse-keeper` on shutdown while a snapshot is being serialized. [#42084](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42084) ([Antonio Andelic](https://github.com/antonio2368)).
* Fix an incorrect result of `bitmapContains` and `bitmapHasAny` when the bitmap is stored as a small set. [#42230](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42230) ([Alexey Milovidov](https://github.com/alexey-milovidov)).
